facts.statement: The genus Longirostravis was described by Hou and colleagues in 2004.
The only known species in the genus is Longirostravis hani.
Longirostravis lived during the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: Longirostravis is a genus of enantiornithean birds which existed during the early Cretaceous period (around 125 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus is known from a single fossil specimen, IVPP V 11309, held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
facts.quote: It is known from a single specimen housed in the collections of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (specimen number IVPP V 11309)

facts.statement: Longirostravis hani was quail-sized and possessed a long, tapering snout with five pairs of small conical teeth.
facts.quote: L. hani appears to have been a "quail-sized" bird with a long, tapering and slightly curved snout tipped with five pairs of small, conical teeth

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the long snout was likely used for mud probing, similar to modern oystercatchers.
facts.quote: The long, narrow snout may have been used for mud probing, an ecology similar to modern oystercatchers

facts.statement: The bird had an unusual sternum featuring three-pronged projections on each side that resembled moose horns.
facts.quote: L. hani had an unusually-shaped breast bone (sternum) with a pair of three-pronged projections shaped somewhat like moose horns on either side

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows feathers covered the body but were absent from the feet and snout.
facts.quote: Feathers were preserved around the entire body but seem to have been absent on the feet and snout

facts.statement: The primary wing feathers reached a maximum length of 8 centimeters.
facts.quote: The primary wing feathers were up to 8 cm in length

facts.statement: Like other enantiornitheans, Longirostravis had a single pair of long feathers on its tail.
facts.quote: As in some other enantiornitheans, the tail sported a single pair of long feathers

facts.statement: Longirostravis is classified within the extinct subclass Enantiornithes.
The genus belongs to the family Longipterygidae.
This extinct genus of enantiornithean birds lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, about 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: Longirostravis es un género extinto de aves enantiornites que vivieron a principios del período Cretácico (hace cerca de 125 millones de años)

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the middle or upper Yixian Formation in Yixian County, China.
facts.quote: es conocida a partir de fósiles hallados en la zona media o superior de la Formación Yixian en el condado Yixian, en la República Popular de China

facts.statement: The species lived between the Barremian and Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The bird's wing feathers were strongly asymmetrical, with the leading edge five times narrower than the trailing edge.
rejected.quote: The wing feathers were strongly asymmetrical, with the leading edge of the feather five times narrower than the trailing edge
